author: raduberinde
body:
#### treesteps: disable in non-invariants mode

Make the treesteps code only active in invariants mode, and add
minimal stubs for non-invariants builds. This will allow using
treesteps for iterators which are performance-sensitive.

#### treesteps: add doc.go


#### treesteps: UpdateLastOpf

Add a convenience function that automatically uses the last op, to
avoid having to plumb the operation through layers of functions.

#### treeprinter: support indented lines under nodes

This change adds the vertical connector when a multi-line node leaves
spaces for it.

#### treeprinter: add DotDotDot

Add a feature to add a vertical ellipsis indicating that a node has
more hidden children.

#### treesteps: deduplicate tree printing code


#### treesteps: improved depth limiting

We improve the way operations are shown when we limit the operation
depth: at the last depth, we show just the result (the last step) of
that operation.

We also use a better representation for the properties so they don't
look like children, and use a vertical ellipsis to indicate hidden
children.

#### treesteps: use best compression level for the URL


#### treesteps: allow passthrough

This change improves tresteps to allow eliding nodes like
`invalidating.Iter` or `keyspan.assertIter` from the hierarchy.

If we simply pass through the `NodeInfo` from the wrapped node, we
still register the elided node instead of the wrapped node (and thus
the wrapped node ops are not recorded). To fix this, we the `Node` to
`NodeInfo`.

Note that passthrough happens implicitly when a node embeds another
node and relies on the embedded `TreeSpepsNode()` implementation (like
`colblk.KeyspanIter` embeds `colblk.keyspanIter`).

author: maciejpirog
body:
# Support for VB.NET part 5 (AST generic)

To make the process of reviewing easier, the support for VB.NET will be added in steps. This is step 5: **AST generic**. This PR merges to the `mpir/vbnet` branch. Only when all parts are reviewed, I will merge it with `main`.

Notes:

1. The parser creates the generic AST directly, with no intermediate data types, so it should be a tiny bit easier on the GC compared to other languages,

2. There are still some todos, marked in the code. They mostly concern complicated but not so important details of types (such as type constraints).

3. LINQ is quite different from the one in C# (see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/6515037/differences-in-linq-syntax-between-vb-net-and-c-sharp), so we cannot simply reuse the code from `Parse_csharp_tree_sitter.ml` to generate AST generic. For now, we keep LINQ as `RawTree` with embedded expression. This allows for matching, not sure yet about tainting. To be fixed ASAP.

4. Only to minimal smoke tests are included. More tests to come in a separate PR (when the rest of the infrastructure is plugged in).

5. This PR also provides some minor tweaks to the lexer and the parser.

author: nineteen17
body:
## Changes

**Architecture:**
- Move type sync script from root to packages/api/scripts/
- Remove root-level type sync infrastructure
- API package now owns and manages type distribution

**Automatic Sync:**
- Types sync automatically on `npm run dev` (API)
- Types sync automatically on `npm run build` (API)
- Manual sync still available: `npm run sync-types` (API)

**Dependencies:**
- Move openapi-typescript to API package devDependencies
- Remove tsx and openapi-typescript from root package.json
- Keep root workspace structure for convenience scripts

**Documentation Updates:**
- README.md: Update type safety workflow to show automatic sync
- TYPE_SAFETY_SETUP.md: Complete rewrite for API-triggered approach
- packages/api/README.md: Document automatic sync behavior
- Remove validate-types script (no longer needed)

**Benefits:**
- ✅ API is source of truth for types
- ✅ Zero manual steps for developers
- ✅ Types sync on every API start/build
- ✅ True package independence (no monorepo confusion)
- ✅ Simpler deployment workflow

Frontend developers: Pull latest changes after API updates to get fresh types

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>coveragepy/coveragepy (coverage)</summary>

### [`v7.11.3`](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.rst#Version-7113--2025-11-09)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/compare/7.11.2...7.11.3)

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement
  core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from
  previous behavior, as reported in `issue 2076`\_ and `issue 2078`\_.

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts
  with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned's `nedbat GitHub account`\_ to
  the `coveragepy GitHub organization`\_. The default branch has changed from
  master to main.

.. \_issue 2076: [#​2076](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2076)
.. \_issue 2078: [#​2078](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2078)
.. \_nedbat GitHub account: <https://github.com/nedbat>
.. \_coveragepy GitHub organization: <https://github.com/coveragepy>

.. \_changes\_7-11-2:

### [`v7.11.2`](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.rst#Version-7112--2025-11-08)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/compare/7.11.1...7.11.2)

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a `NotPython` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`\_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

.. \_issue 2077: [#​2077](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2077)

.. \_changes\_7-11-1:

### [`v7.11.1`](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.rst#Version-7111--2025-11-07)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/compare/7.11.0...7.11.1)

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`\_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`\_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a `breakpoint()` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`\_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option `--debug=core` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split `sqlite` debugging information out of the `sys` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

.. \_issue 1420: [#​1420](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1420)
.. \_issue 2064: [#​2064](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2064)
.. \_issue 2070: [#​2070](https://redirect.github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2070)

#### v2.12.4 (2025-11-05)

This is the fourth 2.12 patch release, fixing more regressions, and reverting a change in the `build()` method
of the [`AnyUrl` and Dsn types](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/api/networks/).

This patch release also fixes an issue with the serialization of IP address types, when `serialize_as_any` is used. The next patch release
will try to address the remaining issues with *serialize as any* behavior by introducing a new *polymorphic serialization* feature, that
should be used in most cases in place of *serialize as any*.

- Fix issue with forward references in parent `TypedDict` classes by [@​Viicos](https://redirect.github.com/Viicos) in [#​12427](https://redirect.github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12427).

  This issue is only relevant on Python 3.14 and greater.
- Exclude fields with `exclude_if` from JSON Schema required fields by [@​Viicos](https://redirect.github.com/Viicos) in [#​12430](https://redirect.github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12430)

  This was initially considered as a bugfix, but caused regressions and as such was fully reverted. The next release will include
  an opt-in option to percent-encode components of the URL.
- Add type inference for IP address types by [@​davidhewitt](https://redirect.github.com/davidhewitt) in [pydantic-core#1868](https://redirect.github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/1868).

  The 2.12 changes to the `serialize_as_any` behavior made it so that IP address types could not properly serialize to JSON.
- Avoid getting default values from defaultdict by [@​davidhewitt](https://redirect.github.com/davidhewitt) in [pydantic-core#1853](https://redirect.github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/1853).

- Add more `pydantic-core` builds for the three-threaded version of Python 3.14 by [@​davidhewitt](https://redirect.github.com/davidhewitt) in [pydantic-core#1864](https://redirect.github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/1864).

author: pyramation
body:
# Enhance CSV loader with streaming parser and quoted identifiers

## Summary
This PR fixes the CSV loader to handle out-of-order columns and adds robust CSV parsing with the `csv-parse` library. The key changes are:

1. **Parse CSV headers and use explicit column list**: Changed from `COPY table FROM STDIN` to `COPY table ("col1", "col2", ...) FROM STDIN` to support CSVs with columns in any order or subset of table columns
2. **Quote all column identifiers**: CSV headers are preserved exactly as-is and quoted in the COPY command, enabling case-sensitive matching between CSV and table columns
3. **Streaming CSV parser**: Uses `csv-parse` with `to_line: 1` to read only the header line, handling BOM, quoted commas, and escaped quotes correctly without loading entire file
4. **Added optional fields to test schemas**: Tests now include nullable columns (email, bio, title, published) to verify CSVs can omit optional columns
5. **Comprehensive edge case tests**: Added tests for quoted commas and escaped quotes in CSV fields

**Important**: Column identifiers are now quoted, so CSV headers must match table column names exactly (case-sensitive). For example, CSV header `User_ID` will only match table column `User_ID`, not `user_id`.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify quoting behavior matches your table schemas**: Since we quote all identifiers, CSV headers must match column names exactly (case-sensitive). Most PostgreSQL tables use lowercase unquoted columns, so CSV headers should be lowercase. Check if any of your tables have mixed-case column names that would require exact case matching.
- [ ] **Test with real CSV files**: Run the loader with actual CSV files from your system to ensure headers match your table schemas. The tests only cover lowercase headers.
- [ ] **Confirm no header cleaning is acceptable**: The implementation no longer normalizes headers (no trim, no lowercase conversion). CSV headers are used exactly as parsed. If your CSVs have trailing spaces or inconsistent casing, PostgreSQL will error.

### Test Plan
```bash
# 1. Start postgres
docker-compose up -d

# 2. Run all CSV tests
cd packages/pgsql-test && yarn test --testPathPattern="csv"

# 3. Test with your own CSV files
# - Create a test with your actual CSV files
# - Verify headers match table column names exactly (case-sensitive)
# - Check that columns can be in any order
```

### Notes
- All 5 CSV tests passing (csv, csv-subset-header, csv-optional-fields, csv-edge-cases with 2 sub-tests)
- The `csv-parse` library handles BOM, CRLF/LF, quoted commas (`"Hello, world!"`), and escaped quotes (`"He said ""hi"""`)
- Removed all header normalization per user request - headers are preserved exactly as-is
- PostgreSQL will error on invalid column names or mismatches, which is the intended behavior
- Session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0efd3785cc294f4a826628b49393619c
- Requested by: Dan Lynch (pyramation@gmail.com) / @pyramation

Pytest 9.0.0 introduced native support for unittest's `self.subTest()` and stricter serialization requirements for subTest parameters when using pytest-xdist parallel execution. Non-serializable objects (mocks, datetime instances, exceptions) passed to `subTest()` now cause `DumpError` failures.

## Changes

- **Upgraded pytest**: 8.4.2 → 9.0.0 in `pyproject.toml`
- **Removed pytest-subtests**: Removed `pytest-subtests==0.14.1` from dev dependencies (pytest 9.0 has native support)
- **Migrated to new TOML config format**: Changed from `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` to `[tool.pytest]` with list-based `addopts`
- **Fixed subTest serialization**: Replaced non-serializable parameters with simple identifiers across 20+ test files

### Pattern Applied

Before:
```python
for case in test_cases:
    with self.subTest(error=case["error"], channel=MockTextChannel()):
        # test logic
```

After:
```python
for i, case in enumerate(test_cases):
    with self.subTest(test_case=i, has_channel=True):
        # test logic
```

### Configuration Migration

Before:
```toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "-p no:nose"
```

After:
```toml
[tool.pytest]
addopts = ["-p", "no:nose"]
```

### Additional Fixes

- Fixed `HTTPException` initialization in `test_utils.py` (requires `message` argument)

All 442 tests pass with xdist parallel execution.

body:
This commit introduces a comprehensive, type-safe Scala 3 wrapper over the
Google GenAI Java SDK, leveraging advanced type system features for maximum
compile-time safety and zero-runtime overhead.

Key Features:

1. Iron Refinement Types
   - Temperature: 0.0-2.0 with compile-time validation
   - TopP: 0.0-1.0 for nucleus sampling
   - TopK: positive integers for token selection
   - MaxOutputTokens, CandidateCount with range constraints
   - String types: ApiKey, ProjectId, Location, MimeType, etc.
   - All constraints validated at compile-time (literals) or runtime (Either)

2. Phantom Types for API Variants
   - GeminiApi vs VertexApi enforced at compile-time
   - Prevents calling Vertex operations on Gemini client (and vice versa)
   - File upload only available in Gemini API
   - Model tuning only available in Vertex AI
   - Type-safe credential handling

3. Capability-Based Model Types
   - Models tagged with capabilities (TextGeneration, ImageGeneration, etc.)
   - Operations require specific capabilities via type constraints
   - Impossible to use text model for image generation at compile-time
   - Type class proofs (HasCapability) for capability checking

4. ADTs for Domain Models
   - Sealed traits for exhaustive pattern matching
   - Role, Part, FinishReason, HarmCategory, etc.
   - Compiler ensures all cases handled
   - No runtime surprises from missing cases

5. Opaque Types for Zero-Cost Abstractions
   - All types erase to primitives at runtime
   - Full type safety at compile-time
   - No primitive obsession
   - Clear, semantic type names

Structure:
- constraints/: Iron type definitions (numeric and string constraints)
- types/: Domain models (ADTs, phantom types, schemas)
- client/: API client with phantom-typed variants
- examples/: Comprehensive usage examples
- DESIGN.md: Detailed design philosophy and patterns
- README.md: Complete usage guide with examples

Benefits:
- Make illegal states unrepresentable
- Fail fast with clear error messages
- Zero runtime overhead
- Self-documenting types
- Refactoring safety
- IDE autocomplete shows only valid operations

This wrapper demonstrates state-of-the-art Scala 3 type system usage for
building ultra-safe, high-performance API clients.

## Changes provided by this PR

This PR optimizes the Dependabot configuration in `.github/dependabot.yml` to improve scheduling and increase the number of allowed concurrent pull requests.

### Problem

Running Dependabot using the monthly schedule results in running the job on the first day of every month. This generates a high load on GitHub systems and causes noticeable delays in running workflows. Additionally, the default limit of 5 open pull requests is often too small, resulting in failing updates due to delayed required updates for some packages.

### Solution

This PR makes the following changes to address these issues:

1. **Randomized Monthly Schedule**: Converts monthly schedules from `interval: monthly` to `interval: cron` with a randomized execution time. The job will now run once a month on a random day (between the 2nd and 28th) at a random time (between 1:00 and 4:00), spreading the load across GitHub systems.

2. **Increased Pull Request Limit**: Sets the `open-pull-requests-limit` to a minimum of 15 (up from the default of 5). This ensures that more dependency updates can be processed simultaneously without blocking critical updates.

3. **Timezone Configuration**: Ensures all schedules use `timezone: Europe/Berlin` for consistent timing.

4. **Multi-directory Support**: If multiple `package.json` files are detected in the repository, the configuration for npm packages is updated to use correct YAML array syntax for `directories` field instead of `directory: "/"` to properly scan all subdirectories. The correct format is:
   ```yaml
   directories:
     - "**/*"
   ```

5. **Syntax Correction**: This PR also corrects any existing invalid `directories: "**/*"` string syntax to the proper YAML array format. The incorrect string syntax is not supported by GitHub Dependabot and must be an array.

### Benefits

- Reduced load on GitHub infrastructure by distributing Dependabot runs across the month
- Faster workflow execution due to reduced system congestion
- More dependency updates can be processed in parallel
- Better handling of repositories with multiple package locations

### Reference

For more information about Dependabot configuration options, see the [GitHub Dependabot Options Reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference).

---

## Deutsche Beschreibung

Diese PR optimiert die Dependabot-Konfiguration in `.github/dependabot.yml`, um die Zeitplanung zu verbessern und die Anzahl der gleichzeitig erlaubten Pull Requests zu erhöhen.

### Problem

Die Ausführung von Dependabot mit monatlichem Zeitplan führt dazu, dass der Job am ersten Tag jedes Monats ausgeführt wird. Dies erzeugt eine hohe Last auf den GitHub-Systemen und verursacht spürbare Verzögerungen bei der Ausführung von Workflows. Zusätzlich ist das Standardlimit von 5 offenen Pull Requests oft zu klein, was zu fehlgeschlagenen Updates führt, da erforderliche Aktualisierungen für einige Pakete verzögert werden.

### Lösung

Diese PR führt die folgenden Änderungen durch, um diese Probleme zu beheben:

1. **Randomisierter monatlicher Zeitplan**: Die monatlichen Zeitpläne werden von `interval: monthly` auf `interval: cron` mit einer zufälligen Ausführungszeit umgestellt. Der Job wird nun einmal im Monat an einem zufälligen Tag (zwischen dem 2. und 28.) zu einer zufälligen Uhrzeit (zwischen 1:00 und 4:00 Uhr) ausgeführt, wodurch die Last auf die GitHub-Systeme verteilt wird.

2. **Erhöhtes Pull-Request-Limit**: Das `open-pull-requests-limit` wird auf mindestens 15 gesetzt (statt dem Standard von 5). Dies stellt sicher, dass mehr Abhängigkeits-Updates gleichzeitig verarbeitet werden können, ohne kritische Updates zu blockieren.

3. **Zeitzonenkonfiguration**: Alle Zeitpläne verwenden `timezone: Europe/Berlin` für eine konsistente Zeitplanung.

4. **Unterstützung mehrerer Verzeichnisse**: Wenn mehrere `package.json`-Dateien im Repository erkannt werden, wird die Konfiguration für npm-Pakete aktualisiert, um die korrekte YAML-Array-Syntax für das `directories`-Feld anstelle von `directory: "/"` zu verwenden, damit alle Unterverzeichnisse ordnungsgemäß gescannt werden. Das korrekte Format ist:
   ```yaml
   directories:
     - "**/*"
   ```

5. **Syntaxkorrektur**: Diese PR korrigiert auch jede vorhandene ungültige `directories: "**/*"` String-Syntax in das richtige YAML-Array-Format. Die falsche String-Syntax wird von GitHub Dependabot nicht unterstützt und muss ein Array sein.

### Vorteile

- Reduzierte Last auf die GitHub-Infrastruktur durch Verteilung der Dependabot-Läufe über den Monat
- Schnellere Workflow-Ausführung aufgrund reduzierter Systemauslastung
- Mehr Abhängigkeits-Updates können parallel verarbeitet werden
- Bessere Handhabung von Repositories mit mehreren Paket-Standorten

### Referenz

Weitere Informationen zu den Dependabot-Konfigurationsoptionen finden sich in der [GitHub Dependabot Options Reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference).

## Scope

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **S‑IDs** | P1 |

### Description

Subprocess output was buffered until completion, causing long-running audit operations to appear hung and accumulating large outputs in memory.

**Changes:**
- Removed `capture_output=True` from `_run_command()` in `cli/status_audit.py` to restore real-time streaming
- Subprocess now inherits parent stdout/stderr, eliminating buffer accumulation
- Updated docstring to clarify streaming behavior

**Before:**
```python
result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
if result.stdout:
    print(result.stdout, end='')
```

**After:**
```python
result = subprocess.run(cmd, text=True)  # Streams directly
```

Commit bcb7773 introduced buffering to make output capturable, but this broke live progress reporting. The test suite already captures CLI-level output correctly, making subprocess-level buffering redundant and harmful.

## Summary

Implements namespace-based authorization for client creation, replacing the token-based authentication system with a declarative grant list approach.

Closes #102

## Breaking Changes ⚠️

- **Realm CRD**: Added required `clientAuthorizationGrants` field
- **Authorization Model**: Removed token-based authorization entirely
- **Migration Required**: Existing realms must add namespace to grant list to allow client creation

## What Changed

### Core Implementation
- ✅ Added `clientAuthorizationGrants` field to KeycloakRealm CRD
- ✅ Implemented namespace format validation (RFC 1123)
- ✅ Updated client reconciler with grant list authorization logic
- ✅ Added `authorizationGranted` status field to KeycloakClient

### RBAC

### Helm Charts (all 3 updated)
- ✅ keycloak-operator: Updated CRD and RBAC

### Tests
- ✅ 6 integration tests (4 new, 2 fixed)

apiVersion: vriesdemichael.github.io/v1

body:
## Description

This PR implements webhook notifier support as requested in #7695, using a reusable webhook infrastructure pattern following Authelia's established configuration conventions.

## Architecture

### Reusable Webhook Infrastructure
Webhooks are defined once in `definitions.webhooks` and can be referenced by multiple features (notifications, future audit logging, telemetry, etc.) - similar to how OIDC authorization policies work.

**Configuration Pattern:**
```yaml
definitions:
  webhooks:
    ntfy:
      url: 'https://ntfy.example.com/authelia'
      method: 'POST'
      timeout: '5s'
      headers:
        Authorization: 'Bearer token123'

notifier:
  webhook_ref: 'ntfy'  # Reference to defined webhook
```

This promotes:
- **Configuration reusability** across multiple Authelia subsystems
- **Consistency** with existing Authelia patterns
- **Future extensibility** for audit logging, telemetry, and other webhook consumers

## Changes

### Webhook Infrastructure (`internal/webhooks`)
- **Reusable HTTP webhook client** for all Authelia subsystems
- HTTPS enforcement (TLS 1.2+ minimum)
- Custom HTTP headers support for authentication
- Configurable HTTP methods (POST, PUT, PATCH)
- Timeout and TLS configuration
- Proper context handling for cancellation/deadlines

### Configuration Schema
- Added `definitions.webhooks` map for reusable webhook definitions
- Added `Webhook` struct with proper koanf tags
- Notifier uses `webhook_ref` to reference defined webhooks
- Configuration validation with HTTPS enforcement
- Mutual exclusivity with SMTP/filesystem notifiers
- Registered webhook configuration keys in schema

### Webhook Notifier Implementation
- Implements Authelia's notifier interface
- JSON payload with schema reference
- Uses existing email templates (plaintext version)
- Proper error handling and logging
- Startup validation

### JSON Schema
- Published formal JSON Schema at `docs/schemas/v1/webhook/notification.json`
- Every webhook payload includes `$schema` field for validation
- Enables automatic type generation for webhook consumers

### Documentation
- Complete webhook definitions guide (`docs/content/configuration/definitions/webhooks.md`)
- Webhook notifier configuration guide (`docs/content/configuration/notifications/webhook.md`)
- Updated notifications introduction to include webhook provider
- Security best practices and integration examples (ntfy, Slack, Discord)

## Compliance with #7695

- ✅ JSON Schema published and referenced in payloads
- ✅ HTTPS strictly enforced
- ✅ Handles user notifications (password reset, TOTP, WebAuthn, etc.)
- ✅ HTTP status code handling (200, 201, 202 accepted)
- ✅ Template-based using existing email templates
- ✅ Consumer adapts to producer schema
- ✅ **Bonus:** Reusable webhook infrastructure for future features

## Testing

- ✅ Container builds successfully
- ✅ All validator tests pass
- ✅ Configuration validation works correctly
- ✅ HTTPS enforcement tested and working
- ✅ Webhook payload structure validated
- ✅ Reference validation (webhook_ref must exist in definitions)

## Webhook Payload Structure

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://github.com/authelia/authelia/blob/master/docs/schemas/v1/webhook/notification.json",

author: mitchellturton
body:
This is the skeleton code for the robosub protobuf based software. This laying out the communications between the PI Picos and the Jetson and general control flow but does not implement any of the actual drivers of interfacing between the Picos and the senors / motors / indicator LED. 

We have two PI Picos, one is Mahikas "Presto Board" which:
1) Controls Motors
2) Has E-Stop
3) Indicator LED
4) Autonomy Switch

The second is Erin's Sensor Board:
1) Voltage and Current Sensing
- Note the skeleton code only has one voltage and current sensor right now but if you give me more context of how many of these sensors and what voltages / currents they measure I can update the framework to handle this
2) Depth / Pressure Sensor

Both of these PI Picos are connected to the Jetson over a dedicated USB connection

Features Added:

Firmware Side:
- Build flags presto_board and sensor_board to select which board you are building / flashing to in PlatformIO
   - Note: This is currently bypassing Sean's CLI. For testing I've been manually building proto messages and building in platformIO directly instead of through the CLI. It simply wasn't built for multiple boards and I didn't feel like adding that feature
 
 - Build Flags -> board_config.h -> pinout.h
    - board_config.h : Takes the overarching board flag and sets smaller feature flags to use in main.cpp
    - pinout.h : Where physical pin interface is defined. Currently completely empty.
       - pins are all under the "pins" namespace. So I would call pins::PICO_STATUS_LED. This is just a personal style preference that can be removed.

- We now have more than one command / telemetry type. However there is no built in way to detect what the type of protobuf message coming in is so I created a high level Envelope protobuf message which allows us to distinguish between the different types.

- I am sending all telemetry data in a single protobuf message type instead of having several smaller protobuf messages

- main.cpp is mostly bare all functions need to be filled in to interact with actual hardware


Software (ROS) Side:
- One node has two driver objects one per Pi Pico
- Nothing too much to talk about in the ros.py just a lot of callbacks and publishers

- I combined _read and _decode 
- Generally refactored a bit to make things more readable
- added more specific command and read functions for our sensors and actuators

Implements spot sell functionality for Bybit exchange that executes market orders and calculates profit/loss against average buy price.

## Changes

**New `SpotSellResult` dataclass**
- Structured return type containing order details, execution price/quantity, and calculated PnL

**New `sell_spot()` method in `BybitExchange`**
- Executes market sell order via Bybit API
- Calculates PnL as `(sell_price - avg_buy_price) × amount`
- Handles missing buy history gracefully (PnL = 0)
- Normalizes symbol format (auto-appends `/USDT`)

**Test coverage**

```python
exchange = BybitExchange(apiKey=key, secret=secret)
order, result = exchange.sell_spot(symbol="BTC", amount=0.5)

# result.price         # Execution price
# result.amount        # Filled quantity
# result.profit_loss   # PnL in USDT
```

- Uses market orders for immediate execution
- PnL calculation silently degrades to 0 if average buy price unavailable
- All symbol inputs normalized to `{SYMBOL}/USDT` format

author: johnjanik
body:
The previous implementation was calling imgui.frame() twice per frame: once in begin_frame() and again in render(), causing the assertion: 'Forgot to call Render() or EndFrame() at the end of the previous frame?'

Changes:
- Refactored ImGuiContext to use a closure-based render() API
- All frame lifecycle steps now happen in a single render() call:
  1. prepare_frame() - update delta time and prepare platform
  2. frame() - begin frame and get UI reference (called once)
  3. build_ui() - user provides closure to build UI
  4. prepare_render() - end frame
  5. render() - render draw data to screen
- Updated main.rs to use the new closure-based API

This ensures proper ImGui frame lifecycle and prevents the core dump.

author: copilot
body:
Implements integration testing infrastructure for ASP.NET Core Web API with SignalR hubs and Redis backplane configuration.

## Implementation

**Test Infrastructure (`SignalRWebApplicationFactory`)**
- Hosts Web API in-memory via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` 
- Manages Redis lifecycle with TestContainers (auto start/stop/cleanup)
- Loads test-specific configuration from `appsettings.IntegrationTests.json`
- Overrides configuration to inject test Redis connection string
- SignalR clients connect through test server's HTTP handler (no network I/O)

**Web API (`src/SignalRWebApi/`)**
- `ChatHub`: Message broadcasting, groups, connection management
- Conditional Redis backplane configuration via `AddStackExchangeRedis`
- `Program` class made accessible to tests via `public partial class Program { }`

**Test Configuration (`appsettings.IntegrationTests.json`)**
- Test-specific logging levels (Debug for SignalR)
- SignalR configuration options (EnableDetailedErrors, KeepAliveInterval)
- Custom test settings (UseTestContainers, TimeoutSeconds)
- Configuration precedence: In-memory overrides > appsettings.IntegrationTests.json > appsettings.json

**Test Coverage (16 tests)**
- SignalR hub functionality: broadcast, groups, join/leave, connections (5 tests)
- Redis operations: connectivity, key-value, pub/sub, multiple connections (5 tests)
- API endpoints: health checks, hub negotiation (2 tests)
- Configuration: loading settings, overrides, accessing values (4 tests)

## Usage

```csharp
// Test fixture automatically manages Redis container
public class ChatHubIntegrationTests : IClassFixture<SignalRWebApplicationFactory>
{
    public async Task InitializeAsync()
    {
        // SignalR client connects to in-memory test server
        _connection = new HubConnectionBuilder()
            .WithUrl($"{httpClient.BaseAddress}chathub", options =>
            {
                options.HttpMessageHandlerFactory = _ => _factory.Server.CreateHandler();
            })
            .Build();
    }
}

// Access configuration in tests
var configuration = _factory.Services.GetRequiredService<IConfiguration>();
var timeoutSeconds = configuration["IntegrationTest:TimeoutSeconds"];
```

Zero external dependencies - TestContainers handles Redis Docker containers. Tests are isolated, repeatable, and CI/CD ready.

## Documentation

- **README.md**: Configuration approach overview
- **USAGE.md**: Running tests, debugging, deployment examples
- **IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md**: Configuration Q&A reference
- **ARCHITECTURE.md**: System diagrams and message flows

author: adamkwhite
body:
## Problem
The rejection risk endpoint was returning "Insufficient data" responses even when the API request included symptom data. This occurred because the frontend sends symptoms in a different format than the agent expects:

**Frontend sends:**
```json
{
  "fever": true,
  "fever_temperature": 101.5,
  "decreased_urine_output": true,
  "tenderness": true
}
```

**Agent expects:**
```json
{
  "fever": 101.5,           // temperature in °F
  "weight_gain": <number>,  // lbs gained  
  "fatigue": <string>,      // description
  "urine_output": <string>  // description
}
```

## Solution
Added `normalize_rejection_symptoms()` function that transforms symptom data:
- `fever_temperature` → `fever` (numeric temperature)
- `decreased_urine_output: true` → `urine_output: "decreased"`
- `fatigue: true` → `fatigue: "moderate"`
- Handles multiple input formats (boolean, numeric, descriptive)

## Files Changed
- `services/missed-dose/main.py:148-215` - New normalizer function
- `services/missed-dose/main.py:461` - Call normalizer before passing to agent

## Testing
Tested normalizer with exact curl request format:
```python
Input: {'fever': True, 'fever_temperature': 101.5, 'decreased_urine_output': True}
Output: {'fever': 101.5, 'urine_output': 'decreased'}
```

All 126 unit tests pass.

## Impact
Fixes production issue where rejection risk analysis couldn't properly assess symptoms, improving patient safety by ensuring accurate risk assessments.

## Changes provided by this PR

This PR optimizes the Dependabot configuration in `.github/dependabot.yml` to improve scheduling and increase the number of allowed concurrent pull requests.

### Problem

Running Dependabot using the monthly schedule results in running the job on the first day of every month. This generates a high load on GitHub systems and causes noticeable delays in running workflows. Additionally, the default limit of 5 open pull requests is often too small, resulting in failing updates due to delayed required updates for some packages.

### Solution

This PR makes the following changes to address these issues:

1. **Randomized Monthly Schedule**: Converts monthly schedules from `interval: monthly` to `interval: cron` with a randomized execution time. The job will now run once a month on a random day (between the 2nd and 28th) at a random time (between 1:00 and 4:00), spreading the load across GitHub systems.

2. **Increased Pull Request Limit**: Sets the `open-pull-requests-limit` to a minimum of 15 (up from the default of 5). This ensures that more dependency updates can be processed simultaneously without blocking critical updates.

3. **Timezone Configuration**: Ensures all schedules use `timezone: Europe/Berlin` for consistent timing.

4. **Multi-directory Support**: If multiple `package.json` files are detected in the repository, the configuration for npm packages is updated to use correct YAML array syntax for `directories` field instead of `directory: "/"` to properly scan all subdirectories. The correct format is:
   ```yaml
   directories:
     - "**/*"
   ```

5. **Syntax Correction**: This PR also corrects any existing invalid `directories: "**/*"` string syntax to the proper YAML array format. The incorrect string syntax is not supported by GitHub Dependabot and must be an array.

### Benefits

- Reduced load on GitHub infrastructure by distributing Dependabot runs across the month
- Faster workflow execution due to reduced system congestion
- More dependency updates can be processed in parallel
- Better handling of repositories with multiple package locations

### Reference

For more information about Dependabot configuration options, see the [GitHub Dependabot Options Reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference).

---

## Deutsche Beschreibung

Diese PR optimiert die Dependabot-Konfiguration in `.github/dependabot.yml`, um die Zeitplanung zu verbessern und die Anzahl der gleichzeitig erlaubten Pull Requests zu erhöhen.

### Problem

Die Ausführung von Dependabot mit monatlichem Zeitplan führt dazu, dass der Job am ersten Tag jedes Monats ausgeführt wird. Dies erzeugt eine hohe Last auf den GitHub-Systemen und verursacht spürbare Verzögerungen bei der Ausführung von Workflows. Zusätzlich ist das Standardlimit von 5 offenen Pull Requests oft zu klein, was zu fehlgeschlagenen Updates führt, da erforderliche Aktualisierungen für einige Pakete verzögert werden.

### Lösung

Diese PR führt die folgenden Änderungen durch, um diese Probleme zu beheben:

1. **Randomisierter monatlicher Zeitplan**: Die monatlichen Zeitpläne werden von `interval: monthly` auf `interval: cron` mit einer zufälligen Ausführungszeit umgestellt. Der Job wird nun einmal im Monat an einem zufälligen Tag (zwischen dem 2. und 28.) zu einer zufälligen Uhrzeit (zwischen 1:00 und 4:00 Uhr) ausgeführt, wodurch die Last auf die GitHub-Systeme verteilt wird.

2. **Erhöhtes Pull-Request-Limit**: Das `open-pull-requests-limit` wird auf mindestens 15 gesetzt (statt dem Standard von 5). Dies stellt sicher, dass mehr Abhängigkeits-Updates gleichzeitig verarbeitet werden können, ohne kritische Updates zu blockieren.

3. **Zeitzonenkonfiguration**: Alle Zeitpläne verwenden `timezone: Europe/Berlin` für eine konsistente Zeitplanung.

4. **Unterstützung mehrerer Verzeichnisse**: Wenn mehrere `package.json`-Dateien im Repository erkannt werden, wird die Konfiguration für npm-Pakete aktualisiert, um die korrekte YAML-Array-Syntax für das `directories`-Feld anstelle von `directory: "/"` zu verwenden, damit alle Unterverzeichnisse ordnungsgemäß gescannt werden. Das korrekte Format ist:
   ```yaml
   directories:
     - "**/*"
   ```

5. **Syntaxkorrektur**: Diese PR korrigiert auch jede vorhandene ungültige `directories: "**/*"` String-Syntax in das richtige YAML-Array-Format. Die falsche String-Syntax wird von GitHub Dependabot nicht unterstützt und muss ein Array sein.

### Vorteile

- Reduzierte Last auf die GitHub-Infrastruktur durch Verteilung der Dependabot-Läufe über den Monat
- Schnellere Workflow-Ausführung aufgrund reduzierter Systemauslastung
- Mehr Abhängigkeits-Updates können parallel verarbeitet werden
- Bessere Handhabung von Repositories mit mehreren Paket-Standorten

### Referenz

Weitere Informationen zu den Dependabot-Konfigurationsoptionen finden sich in der [GitHub Dependabot Options Reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference).

Hi Dropback!

Had a blast doing the take home assignment.

Can view a quick loom sample here: https://www.loom.com/share/d7193d27e46a48bd944c4ef0970f57df

NOTE:
- for set up you will have to copy/paste the .env.example to .env.local and add in the supabase key and url
- npm install
- run the /api/data-ingestion to load the data into the db
- localhost:3000 to see the changes

Backend Implementation details:
- Used the ESPN API to pull men's college basketball statistics for the 2025 season
- Using the given `apps/web/app/api/data-ingestion/route.ts` route I used this to pull the player data and the player's statistics into the supabase database
- I used a .env.local file to store the credential information, and urls and then used supabase client
- The basketball API splits the data into the home and away datasets, in this case I stored both, first mapping the data first and then stored the statistics. The player_stats table has espn_player_id that references the id in the player table this is how the two tables are related. It also has an index `idx_player_stats_comparison` which uses split_type and season as comparisons, it wasn't used because I didn't include filtering on the frontend but would be useful.
- For querying I created some separate api routes, some I ended up not using in the final implementation but would be useful (for example getting stats by id). The GET players/ is the main api I used to fetch the players in the database. The GET players/compare was the API I used to fetch multiple player statistics.
- Tried to use TypeScript typing (interfaces, enum) as much as I could

Frontend implementation details:
- Kept it simple and mainly only added two additional dependencies `recharts` for data visualization and `swr` for data fetching (https://swr.vercel.app/docs/data-fetching)
- The dropdown component is in the takehome/ui folder as it could be reused, it fetches the players and renders them
- The state is then held in the page component to be used by the home statistics, now this is very simple we could have instead used a query param/ navigation/ router solution but didn't seem necessary at this point in time
- When the second selection is made, the comparison table and the visualizations table are rendered
- The statistics comparison takes the player ids and fetches the stats from the api, it then renders the home/away data separately
- The data visualization uses recharts barchart to show a visual comparison between the two players, I've also added a toggle between their home/away statistics. Alternatively the home/away could be fed into the api to gather the data back.
- Alternatively the player statistics table and the data visualization could be grouped together to only run the statistics api once to get the data back.

Some alternatives:
- Alternatively for the barchart the home/away selection could be fed into the api to gather the data back.
- Alternatively the player statistics table and the data visualization could be grouped together to only run the statistics api once to get the data back. In this case I wanted to separate the component out and for each component to be independent. 

With more time I would:
- clean out the api/actions and api/players/ a bit more
- add testing support (jest, or other)
- combine the home/away stats together into a averaged statistic

author: marcoroth
body:
This pull request fixes a critical performance regression in the two-pass tag matching algorithm introduced in #795.

Documents that previously parsed in ~75ms were taking ~11 seconds (and in some cases didn't even complete in a reasonable timeframe, see #828).

The `match_tags_visitor` function was causing double recursion by manually processing array fields through calls to `match_tags_in_node_array()`, but then returning `true` which instructed `herb_visit_node` to also automatically traverse those same children a second time.

This created an exponential explosion where each level of nesting squared the number of visits.

Resolves #828

body:
## Why I'm doing:
For OLAP tables, table cardinality can be obtained from three sources: table statistics, partition row count, and basic meta.

1. **Table statistics**: Statistics collection populates table statistics. This can be triggered through manual ANALYZE, background automatic analyze, and data loading.

2. **Partition row count**: Obtained through tablet meta stats in the table.

3. **Basic meta**: Records the number of data rows for each load operation at the table level.

After a user performs an overwrite table operation with `enable_statistic_collect_on_first_load` disabled, if a query is executed immediately after loading:

1. Since overwrite creates a new partition, there will be no statistics for that partition in table statistics.

2. Partition row count is obtained through tablet stats. Tablet stats collection is asynchronous on both FE and BE sides. Each BE and leader FE collect stats every 5 minutes by default. That is, BE collects all tablet information in the BE node's cache every 5 minutes, then FE accesses all BE nodes every 5 minutes to retrieve tablet information. If the partition's publish version time is later than the tablet reporting time, we use the table-level row count recorded in BasicMeta for rough estimation. If the publish version time is earlier than the FE tablet reporting time, we use partition row count for calculation.

However, there's an issue here: if the BE hasn't collected tablet stats for its local node yet, but the FE sends a request to retrieve tablet stats, the obtained tablet row count will be 0.

To prevent this extreme case, we implement an adaptation here.

NOTE: This PR depends on https://git.toradex.com/cgit/meta-toradex-bsp-common.git/commit/?h=scarthgap-7.x.y&id=df1b539e6d9144aa20e3d25e09fc1082346aa07e

----

This PR adds two new optional user-configurable variables to the `tdx-tezi-data-partition` bbclass, providing greater flexibility when configuring data partitions in Toradex Easy Installer images.

### Changes
1. `TDX_TEZI_DATA_PARTITION_WANT_MAXIMIZED` variable
    - Allows users to control whether the data partition should be maximized to use all available space
    - Set to `"1"` (default) to maximize the partition - if multiple partitions share this setting, remaining space is distributed evenly
    - Set to `"0"` to use only the nominal size
    - Maintains backward compatibility with default value of "1"
2. `TDX_TEZI_DATA_PARTITION_SIZE_NOMINAL` variable
    - Allows users to specify the nominal size of the data partition in MB
    - When `TDX_TEZI_DATA_PARTITION_WANT_MAXIMIZED = "0"`, this is the actual partition size
    - When `TDX_TEZI_DATA_PARTITION_WANT_MAXIMIZED = "1"`, this serves as the minimum size
    - Defaults to "512" (512 MB) for backward compatibility

### Use Case
These variables are particularly useful when:
- You need a fixed-size data partition for deterministic storage allocation
- You want to reserve space for other partitions or future expansion
- You need to control partition sizes for testing or specific deployment requirements

### Example Configuration
```
INHERIT += "tdx-tezi-data-partition"
TDX_TEZI_DATA_PARTITION_SIZE_NOMINAL = "1024"      # 1GB partition
TDX_TEZI_DATA_PARTITION_WANT_MAXIMIZED = "0"       # Don't maximize
```

author: neillamoureux
body:
## Summary

### Qt replaced with wx
This PR replaces the Qt UI framework (using Pyside6), with wxPython.  

Pyside6 is quite large: looking at the install at .venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages: we find (on macos):

- On the main branch:
    - pyside6: 1,481,185,792 bytes (1.58 GB on disk) for 18,329 items
    - pyside6 alone: 1,236,972,373 bytes (1.26 GB on disk) for 5,052 items
 
- On the feat/wx branch:
    - with wx installed, this directory has a size of: 331,651,649 bytes (417 MB on disk) for 14,734 items
    - wx directory alone: 65,392,583 bytes (67.2 MB on disk) for 584 items

So the wx branch install is more than 1 GB smaller and only about 25% of the size of the install with Pyside6.

Also, generally I found working with wx a little simpler.

### Use of Observable to update UI
I had issues ensuring that the UI was properly synced up to the view; for example, the camera type selected in the UI would often be wrong, or the menu version vs the radio button version would be different.  To fix this, I used the Observable class so the when the state changes in the view (eg the camera type changes), the UI is updated.

### Action class
Two or more UI elements can do the same thing; for example, the user can show or hide the axes from a button or the menu.  To ensure these different controls did the same thing, and showed the same state, I created the Action class and its subclasses.  The define what function to run when the control is used, and in the subclasses, the observable to subscribe to for updates on state. Only enough was written to satify the needs of this program.

### Subprocess to run "loaded module"
The user selects "Load .py" to load the code the creates the mesh via a `create_mesh` function.  To keep the UI more fluid, this is now run in a subprocess.  Before it was run in a thread, and due to Python's GIL, it could be very choppy when loading.  
 
The threaded version used callbacks to indicate the status of the load, but the subprocess version uses a command queue to send commands to the subprocess.  Only one subprocess is created so that things like the available fonts remain in its memory.  But each load creates a new thread in the subprocess.

The threaded version also used a queue to send meshes to the main thread.  In this version, the queue contains `LoadResult`, which has the mesh plus other info such as whether this is the final mesh from `create_mesh`.

3. **Basic meta**: Records the number of data rows for each load operation at the table level.

After a user performs an overwrite table operation with `enable_statistic_collect_on_first_load` disabled, if a query is executed immediately after loading:

1. Since overwrite creates a new partition, there will be no statistics for that partition in table statistics.

2. Partition row count is obtained through tablet stats. Tablet stats collection is asynchronous on both FE and BE sides. Each BE and leader FE collect stats every 5 minutes by default. That is, BE collects all tablet information in the BE node's cache every 5 minutes, then FE accesses all BE nodes every 5 minutes to retrieve tablet information. If the partition's publish version time is later than the tablet reporting time, we use the table-level row count recorded in BasicMeta for rough estimation. If the publish version time is earlier than the FE tablet reporting time, we use partition row count for calculation.

However, there's an issue here: if the BE hasn't collected tablet stats for its local node yet, but the FE sends a request to retrieve tablet stats, the obtained tablet row count will be 0.

To prevent this extreme case, we implement an adaptation here.

author: sundargthb
body:
## Description

This PR enhances the AgentCore Code Interpreter integration to support **automatic session persistence and reconnection** across invocations in long-running AgentCore runtimes. This eliminates session lifecycle mismatches, prevents tool execution failures, and significantly improves performance.


Implement automatic session lifecycle management and cross-invocation session 
reconnection for AgentCore Code Interpreter integration. This enhancement enables 
sessions to persist across invocations in long-running AgentCore runtimes, 
eliminating session recreation overhead and preventing tool execution failures.

Key changes:
- Add persist_sessions flag to prevent premature session cleanup
- Add verify_session_before_use flag for session verification and reconnection
- Implement list_sessions()-based session discovery for cross-instance reconnection
- Add session name validation and cleaning for AWS CodeInterpreter constraints
- Store session name-to-ID mapping for reliable session lookup

This resolves session lifecycle mismatches between short-lived Python objects
and long-lived AgentCore sessions, improving performance by 69-72% and achieving
0% tool failure rate in multi-turn conversations.

Fixes: Session validation errors and unnecessary session recreation
Related: AgentCore runtime integration, Strands Agent framework

## 🎯 Problem Statement

### The Session Lifecycle Mismatch

**AgentCore Runtime Architecture:**
- Long-running Python process that persists across invocations
- Each user request triggers a new `@app.entrypoint` function call
- Code Interpreter sessions are designed to persist across these invocations

**Previous Integration Behavior:**
- New `AgentCoreCodeInterpreter` instance created on every invocation
- Python object destruction triggered `__del__()` → session cleanup
- Next invocation had no knowledge of previous sessions
- Resulted in continuous session creation/destruction cycle

## ✅ Solution Overview

This PR implements three key enhancements:

### 1. **Session Persistence Control**
Add `persist_sessions` flag (default: `True`) to prevent session cleanup on object destruction.

### 2. **Session Verification and Reconnection**
Add `verify_session_before_use` flag (default: `True`) to verify and reconnect to existing sessions.

### 3. **Session Discovery Mechanism**
Use `list_sessions()` API with name matching to find and reconnect to existing sessions across object instances.


## Type of Change

New Tool


## Testing

How have you tested the change?  Verify that the changes do not break functionality or introduce warnings in consuming repositories: agents-docs, agents-tools, agents-cli

- [ x] I ran `hatch run prepare`
### Test Scenarios Validated:

1. **First invocation creates session:**
   ```
   ✅ Session created with cleaned name
   ✅ Session ID stored
   ✅ Tool execution successful
   ```

2. **Second invocation reconnects:**
   ```
   ✅ list_sessions() called
   ✅ Session found by name
   ✅ Reconnected to existing session
   ✅ No new session created
   ✅ Tool execution successful
   ```

3. **Session name validation:**
   ```
   Input:  "16e4dcba-5792-4643-9e54-42b43dc58637"
   Output: "16e4dcba579246439e5442b43dc58637"
   ✅ Meets validation: [0-9a-zA-Z]{1,40}
   ```

4. **Session not found handling:**
   ```
   ✅ list_sessions() returns no match
   ✅ Falls back to auto_create
   ✅ New session created successfully
   ```

5. **Session cleanup (when persist_sessions=False):**
   ```
   ✅ Verifies session status before stopping
   ✅ Skips already-stopped sessions
   ✅ No errors from double-stop attempts
   ```

body:
This pull request sets up the initial frontend architecture for the Plataforma de Evaluación Crediticia, focusing on implementing a robust authentication module and preparing the codebase for further development. It introduces a React + TypeScript + Vite stack, provides mock data for users and business entities, and establishes routing, global authentication context, and protected dashboard access. Documentation is added to guide usage and future expansion.

**Authentication & Routing**

* Implements global authentication context (`AuthContext`) with login, registration (auto-login), logout, and session persistence in `localStorage`. Roles are supported for conditional rendering and route protection. (`src/context/AuthContext.tsx`, `src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-26ad4b834941d9b19ebf9db8082bd202aaf72ea0ddea85f5a8a0cb3c729cc6f2R1-R39) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-18818acbefb343d45b10cdd411ea121ebbf4b9dee1824a3dc449fa1bdbbb29f9R1-R89) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3c697fd2fc383be33e306936351fb54033c81a65d7fef747906f76f3b25ac5c7R1-R24)
* Sets up protected routes using `ProtectedRoute` and React Router, distinguishing between public (login, register, recover) and protected (dashboard) pages. (`src/App.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c697fd2fc383be33e306936351fb54033c81a65d7fef747906f76f3b25ac5c7R1-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-26ad4b834941d9b19ebf9db8082bd202aaf72ea0ddea85f5a8a0cb3c729cc6f2R1-R39)

**Mock Data & Domain Modeling**

* Adds mock data for users, clients, requests, and evaluations, modeling key business entities and enabling simulated flows for authentication and dashboard display. (`src/data/mockData.ts`, [src/data/mockData.tsR1-R104](diffhunk://#diff-a0911d4fbda923b2093cec8fc7f76ece04d5e7fef99bd09af0516057862996a9R1-R104))
* Defines TypeScript types/interfaces for domain entities and context contracts, supporting type safety across modules. (`src/types/`, referenced in context and data files)

**Project Structure & Styling**

* Establishes modular folder structure (`src/assets`, `components`, `context`, `data`, `hooks`, `pages`, `styles`, `types`) and basic global/page-specific styles for a clean, responsive UI. (`README.md`, `CREDENCIALES.md`, `src/App.css`, `src/index.css`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-60f5dcfc15327d5dd812d9df394c217efbedb4aa33dca782ed69d39dce811972R1-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-85da366246340e911d7a0eb9153e64137a1b31f0686c74d9aef9ae4f032cb09eR1-R21)

**Tooling & Documentation**

* Adds ESLint configuration and scripts for development, build, preview, and linting; documents project setup, folder organization, and usage of mock credentials. (`package.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `README.md`, `CREDENCIALES.md`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R1-R32) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a32a0887ed9d1d707bbb3b845b7df7fd40e673c47e7b60a3ebd896b68d3b8839R1-R23) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-24771a715321e676c4c3761e67024d77e5f3d1521c2c648914be24ed91d13a03R1-R88) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a32a0887ed9d1d707bbb3b845b7df7fd40e673c47e7b60a3ebd896b68d3b8839R1-R23)

body:
User reported all flows in an environment were deleted after accidentally enabling "CLEANUP - Admin | Sync Template v4 (Check Deleted)" flow. PowerShell restoration attempts fail with "Workflow not found" error.

## Key Findings

**CLEANUP flow behavior clarification:**
- Does NOT delete actual flows from Power Platform environments
- Only marks flows as deleted in CoE Dataverse inventory tables
- Optionally removes records from CoE tables based on "Also Delete From CoE" environment variable

**"Workflow not found" error indicates:**
- Flows were actually deleted from Power Platform (not just marked deleted in CoE)
- Permanent deletion - no PowerShell/API recovery possible
- No recycle bin exists for deleted flows (unlike Dataverse records)

## Recovery Options Provided

1. **Verify actual state** - Flows may still exist in environment, only marked deleted in CoE inventory
2. **Manual CoE inventory fix** - Update `admin_Flows` table deleted flag if flows exist
3. **Solution backup restoration** - If flows were packaged and exported
4. **Environment backup** - Full environment restore via Microsoft Support
5. **Recreation** - Last resort if permanently deleted without backups

## Documentation Created

Comprehensive answer document (`/tmp/issue_10441_answer.md`) includes:
- Detailed explanation of CLEANUP flow behavior
- Step-by-step recovery procedures
- Prevention strategies (solution exports, backups, proper CLEANUP configuration)
- Links to related GitHub issues (#9401, #8866, #8693)
- Microsoft Learn documentation references

No code changes made per agent instructions - this is a question/support issue requiring clarification and guidance.

author: n-onorato
body:
Major improvements for better agent usability:

1. **Simplified output format**:
   - Changed from `response_format: "concise"|"detailed"` to `format: "text"|"json"`
   - Default is now "text" (human-readable log format)
   - "json" returns structured data for programmatic use

2. **Log-style text output** (default):
   - Each place shown on its own line for easy parsing
   - Format: `- <location> (<lat>, <lng>) "<name>" <distance> meters [fields]`
   - Example: `- 123 Main St (37.7, -122.4) "Starbucks" 250 meters [rating: 4.5]`

3. **Better list input support**:
   - `feature_types` now accepts both single string and list of strings
   - Makes it easier for agents to use without worrying about list syntax

4. **Category support**:
   - Can now search by category names (e.g., "food_drink", "sports")
   - Categories automatically expand to all place types in that category
   - `list_place_types()` now accepts single or multiple categories
   - Example: `feature_types=["food_drink", "park"]` searches all food/drink places + parks

5. **Consistent interface across all tools**:
   - All tools (distance_matrix, nearby_search, batch_nearby_search) use same pattern
   - Same `format` parameter, same output structure
   - Same support for single string or list inputs where applicable

Updated documentation in README.md and CLAUDE.md to reflect these changes.

Se añadieron utilidades y estilos en styles/global.css bajo @layer components para homogeneizar la UI. ## Beneficios - Mejor rendimiento y experiencia SSR-friendly al servir la fuente con next/font. - Menor dependencia de recursos externos y mayor control de caching. - Consistencia visual y reutilización de estilos mediante utilidades centralizadas. - Menos solicitudes HTTP por iconos embebidos (data URI). ## Verificación (checklist para merge) - This PR significantly enhances the environment variable management system and converts configuration pages to interactive client components, providing a much better user experience for managing project settings.

### Key Features Added

**🔐 Complete Secrets Management**
- Full CRUD operations for project secrets and environment variables
- Support for categorized variables (auth, payment, general, secret)

**⚙️ Interactive Configuration Pages**
- **Auth Configuration**: Tabbed interface for GitHub OAuth, Google OAuth, and NextAuth settings
- **Payment Configuration**: Structured forms for Stripe and PayPal provider setup

**🐛 Critical Bug Fixes**
- Fixed data loss bug in environment variable batch update operations
- Fixed display issues with environment variables by category
- Proper Prisma type usage throughout the application

### Technical Improvements

- Converted server-side components to interactive client components
- Added proper state management and loading states
- Implemented secret visibility toggles and form validation
- Enhanced UX with better error handling and visual feedback

- `app/projects/[id]/secrets/page.tsx` - Enhanced secrets management with proper types

author: shanemmattner
body:
## Summary
Fixes a TypeError that occurred when using ComponentCollection.get() or remove() methods with component references. The bug was caused by a mismatch between the non-unique reference index configuration and the methods attempting to use the index value directly as an integer.

## Problem
User reported this error when running basic example code:
```
TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not list
  File "kicad_sch_api/collections/components.py", line 1145, in get
    return self._items[ref_idx]
```

The issue occurred in:
- `add_wire_between_pins("R1", "2", "C1", "1")` 
- Any other code path calling `components.get(reference)`

## Root Cause
The ComponentCollection reference index was intentionally set to `unique=False` (line 670) to support multi-unit components like op-amps (TL072 with U1A, U1B, etc.). 

When `unique=False`, the IndexRegistry.get() method returns a **list of indices** instead of a single integer. However, both get() and remove() methods were attempting to use this list directly as an array index: `self._items[ref_idx]`, causing a TypeError.

## Changes
- **get() method** (lines 1145-1153): Added list handling logic
- **remove() method** (lines 1059-1067): Added list handling logic

Both methods now:
- Check if the returned index is a list
- Extract the first element when multiple components share the same reference
- Maintain backward compatibility if the index becomes unique in the future

## Testing
✅ User's original failing code now works:
```python
sch = ksa.create_schematic("My Circuit")
sch.components.add(lib_id="Device:R", reference="R1", value="10k", position=(100, 100))
sch.components.add(lib_id="Device:C", reference="C1", value="100nF", position=(150, 100))
wire_uuid = sch.add_wire_between_pins("R1", "2", "C1", "1")  # Now works!
```

✅ Test suite:
- Fixed 7 failing tests related to this bug
- No new regressions introduced  
- 1142 tests passing

## Related Issues
This appears to be a regression from a previous fix attempt that was reverted (commit 876d1ae).

body:
- Resolve issue where zero values (0, "", false) could not be scanned into pointer fields
- Ensure proper handling of both NULL values and actual zero values
- Update pointer field assignment logic in unmarshal/getValueInterface functions


## Description
This PR fixes a critical issue in the `getValueInterface` function within `sqlx` where NULL values and zero values from the database were not being correctly scanned into destination struct fields.

### The Problem
Previously, when unmarshaling database rows into Go structs:
- **NULL values** could not be properly assigned to basic non-pointer fields (e.g., `string`, `int`)
- **Zero values** (empty string `""`, number `0`, `false`) had incorrect behavior when scanning into pointer fields
- The distinction between actual NULL values and intentional zero values was not maintained

### The Solution
Enhanced the `getValueInterface` function in `sqlx/orm.go` to properly handle:
- Conversion of database NULL values to the zero value of destination basic types
- Correct allocation and assignment of zero values to pointer fields
- Proper distinction between NULL (sets pointer to `nil`) and zero values (allocates pointer to zero value)

### Tests Added
Comprehensive test coverage added in `sqlx/orm_test.go`:

#### 1. Pointer Field Handling
- **`TestUnmarshalRowsZeroValueStructPtr`**: Tests zero values and NULL values in mixed pointer/non-pointer structs
- **`TestUnmarshalRowsAllNullStructPtrFields`**: Tests all-NULL scenarios for pointer-only structs

#### 2. SQL Null Types
- **`TestUnmarshalRowsWithSqlNullTypes`**: Tests all `sql.Null` types (String, Int64, Float64, Bool) with NULL values
- **`TestUnmarshalRowsSqlNullWithMixedData`**: Tests mixed basic types and sql.Null types
- **`TestUnmarshalRowsSqlNullTime`**: Specialized test for `sql.NullTime` type

#### 3. Edge Cases and Zero Value Scenarios
- **`TestUnmarshalRowsSqlNullWithEmptyValues`**: Distinguishes between empty values and NULL values
- **`TestUnmarshalRowsSqlNullStringEmptyVsNull`**: Specifically tests empty string vs NULL string handling

### Test Coverage
The new tests validate:
- ✅ NULL → zero value conversion for basic types
- ✅ NULL → `nil` for pointer fields  
- ✅ Zero values → allocated pointers with correct values
- ✅ All `sql.Null*` types handle NULL correctly
- ✅ Mixed structs with both pointer and non-pointer fields
- ✅ Time types with `sql.NullTime`
- ✅ Empty strings vs NULL strings distinction

### Changes
1. **Core Fix**: Refactored `sqlx/orm.go::getValueInterface` function
2. **Tests**: Added 7 comprehensive test functions with multiple test cases
3. **Validation**: All existing tests continue to pass

### Impact
- Prevents data loss when scanning NULL values into structs
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing code
- Provides robust handling for database NULL semantics

#### 📝 Explanation and details


The optimized version achieves a **40% speedup** by eliminating the expensive `timetuple()` call and slice operation from the original implementation.

**Key optimization:**
- **Original approach**: `dt.datetime(*obj.timetuple()[:6], tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)` creates a full `struct_time` tuple (9 elements), slices it to get the first 6 elements, then unpacks them into the datetime constructor.

## Changes provided by this PR

This PR optimizes the Dependabot configuration in `.github/dependabot.yml` to improve scheduling and increase the number of allowed concurrent pull requests.

### Problem

Running Dependabot using the monthly schedule results in running the job on the first day of every month. This generates a high load on GitHub systems and causes noticeable delays in running workflows. Additionally, the default limit of 5 open pull requests is often too small, resulting in failing updates due to delayed required updates for some packages.

### Solution

This PR makes the following changes to address these issues:

1. **Randomized Monthly Schedule**: Converts monthly schedules from `interval: monthly` to `interval: cron` with a randomized execution time. The job will now run once a month on a random day (between the 2nd and 28th) at a random time (between 1:00 and 4:00), spreading the load across GitHub systems.

2. **Increased Pull Request Limit**: Sets the `open-pull-requests-limit` to a minimum of 15 (up from the default of 5). This ensures that more dependency updates can be processed simultaneously without blocking critical updates.

3. **Timezone Configuration**: Ensures all schedules use `timezone: Europe/Berlin` for consistent timing.

4. **Multi-directory Support**: If multiple `package.json` files are detected in the repository, the configuration for npm packages is updated to use correct YAML array syntax for `directories` field instead of `directory: "/"` to properly scan all subdirectories. The correct format is:
   ```yaml
   directories:
     - "**/*"
   ```

5. **Syntax Correction**: This PR also corrects any existing invalid `directories: "**/*"` string syntax to the proper YAML array format. The incorrect string syntax is not supported by GitHub Dependabot and must be an array.

### Benefits

- Reduced load on GitHub infrastructure by distributing Dependabot runs across the month
- Faster workflow execution due to reduced system congestion
- More dependency updates can be processed in parallel
- Better handling of repositories with multiple package locations

### Reference

For more information about Dependabot configuration options, see the [GitHub Dependabot Options Reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference).

## Deutsche Beschreibung

Diese PR optimiert die Dependabot-Konfiguration in `.github/dependabot.yml`, um die Zeitplanung zu verbessern und die Anzahl der gleichzeitig erlaubten Pull Requests zu erhöhen.

### Problem

Die Ausführung von Dependabot mit monatlichem Zeitplan führt dazu, dass der Job am ersten Tag jedes Monats ausgeführt wird. Dies erzeugt eine hohe Last auf den GitHub-Systemen und verursacht spürbare Verzögerungen bei der Ausführung von Workflows. Zusätzlich ist das Standardlimit von 5 offenen Pull Requests oft zu klein, was zu fehlgeschlagenen Updates führt, da erforderliche Aktualisierungen für einige Pakete verzögert werden.

### Lösung

Diese PR führt die folgenden Änderungen durch, um diese Probleme zu beheben:

1. **Randomisierter monatlicher Zeitplan**: Die monatlichen Zeitpläne werden von `interval: monthly` auf `interval: cron` mit einer zufälligen Ausführungszeit umgestellt. Der Job wird nun einmal im Monat an einem zufälligen Tag (zwischen dem 2. und 28.) zu einer zufälligen Uhrzeit (zwischen 1:00 und 4:00 Uhr) ausgeführt, wodurch die Last auf die GitHub-Systeme verteilt wird.

2. **Erhöhtes Pull-Request-Limit**: Das `open-pull-requests-limit` wird auf mindestens 15 gesetzt (statt dem Standard von 5). Dies stellt sicher, dass mehr Abhängigkeits-Updates gleichzeitig verarbeitet werden können, ohne kritische Updates zu blockieren.

3. **Zeitzonenkonfiguration**: Alle Zeitpläne verwenden `timezone: Europe/Berlin` für eine konsistente Zeitplanung.

4. **Unterstützung mehrerer Verzeichnisse**: Wenn mehrere `package.json`-Dateien im Repository erkannt werden, wird die Konfiguration für npm-Pakete aktualisiert, um die korrekte YAML-Array-Syntax für das `directories`-Feld anstelle von `directory: "/"` zu verwenden, damit alle Unterverzeichnisse ordnungsgemäß gescannt werden. Das korrekte Format ist:
   ```yaml
   directories:
     - "**/*"
   ```

5. **Syntaxkorrektur**: Diese PR korrigiert auch jede vorhandene ungültige `directories: "**/*"` String-Syntax in das richtige YAML-Array-Format. Die falsche String-Syntax wird von GitHub Dependabot nicht unterstützt und muss ein Array sein.

### Vorteile

author: copilot
body:
The CPS transformer failed to handle plain assignments with `await` inside loops (e.g., `x = await expr()`), causing promise chains to break and continuations to never execute. Only variable declarations (`let x = await expr()`) were properly transformed.

## Changes

**CpsTransformer.cs**
- Added case in `TransformStatementWithAwait` to detect pattern `(expr-stmt (assign var (await promise)))`
- Transforms plain assignments into promise chains: extracts await expression, creates `.then()` callback with temporary variable, performs assignment inside callback, chains continuation

## Example

Before this fix, the second `await` in loops would silently fail:

```javascript
async function test() {
    let iterator = str[Symbol.iterator]();
    let result = await iterator.next();  // ✅ works (variable declaration)
    
    while (!result.done) {
        result = await iterator.next();  // ❌ broken (plain assignment)
    }
}
```

The fix ensures both forms transform correctly into promise chains, maintaining continuation flow through loop iterations.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> final failing test.
> 
> go at it:
> 
> I've investigated the ForAwaitOf_WithString_ManualAsyncIteration test failure. This is a pre-existing issue not caused by my changes - I verified the test fails identically on the base commit (cadfa46).
> 
> The test fails at line 289 (iterResult = await iterator.next()) inside the while loop. The logs show:
> 
> "About to call next" is printed
> "Next result" is never printed
> Only "h" is captured instead of "hello"
> The issue appears to be with how the CPS transformation handles await on synchronous iterator methods inside loops. The first await iterator.next() outside the loop (line 282) works fine, but subsequent calls inside the while loop don't complete.
> 
> This is indeed a sync vs async iterator issue - strings have synchronous iterators, and awaiting a sync iterator's .next() method within a loop context seems to break the promise chain continuation.
> 
> Since this is unrelated to the try-catch execution order fix I implemented, it should be tracked as a separate issue.


</details>

author: jakehukari
body:
Root cause: When a player respawns, RebuildESP creates new (invisible) drawing objects, but the update accumulator isn't reset. For far players, this means Update() won't be called for up to 0.1 seconds, leaving old nametags visible and frozen at the respawn location.

Solution: Call ResetESPCounters() after RebuildESP to reset the update accumulator. This forces Update() to run on the next frame, immediately hiding old nametags and showing new ones at the correct position.

This ensures smooth nametag transitions during respawn with no visual artifacts.

Previously, these functions would not evaluate when given numeric arguments, unlike other functions in the same module ([exp2](cci:2://file:///Users/ayushkumarjha/Desktop/sympy/sympy/codegen/cfunctions.py:175:0-224:29), [log2](cci:2://file:///Users/ayushkumarjha/Desktop/sympy/sympy/codegen/cfunctions.py:223:0-280:53), [log10](cci:2://file:///Users/ayushkumarjha/Desktop/sympy/sympy/codegen/cfunctions.py:340:0-386:53), [expm1](cci:2://file:///Users/ayushkumarjha/Desktop/sympy/sympy/codegen/cfunctions.py:20:0-78:37), [log1p](cci:2://file:///Users/ayushkumarjha/Desktop/sympy/sympy/codegen/cfunctions.py:85:0-160:42)).

The optimization primarily targets the `_validate_prompt_template` function by addressing two key performance bottlenecks:

2. **Eliminated list comprehension allocation**: Replaced the list comprehension that collected all format arguments with a generator-based approach that processes fields one-by-one. This avoids creating an intermediate list and enables early termination as soon as validation fails.

3. **Short-circuit validation logic**: Instead of parsing all fields and then comparing the result list, the optimized version validates each field immediately during iteration. If a second field is found or if any field isn't "prompt", it raises an exception immediately without processing remaining fields.

**Why This Leads to Speedups:**

- **Memory efficiency**: Eliminates the temporary list allocation from the original `format_args = [...]` comprehension
- **Early termination**: Stops processing as soon as an invalid condition is detected, rather than parsing the entire template
- **Cache-friendly**: The exact string comparison for `"{prompt}"` is extremely fast and avoids object allocation entirely
- **Reduced function calls**: Fewer calls to the formatter's parsing machinery for common cases

**Performance Impact by Test Case:**
The optimization shows consistent improvements across all test scenarios, with particularly strong gains for:
- Exact `"{prompt}"` templates: 348% faster
